document_multiplayer_create: Choose a game when creating a room, then share the room code or invite link with your friends.
document_multiplayer_ready: Take a player seat, choose a character, and ready up. The other players wait for the host to start the game.
document_multiplayer_coopIntro: If you know the original games, you can jump right in. Play a few runs or browse the quick chat messages to learn most co-op mechanics.
document_multiplayer_coopGuide: Read the guide below for more details.
document_multiplayer_versusIntro: Versus games work differently. Start with a tutorial to get familiar with the mechanics before your first match.
document_multiplayer_challengeSummary: Bombs are disabled, players respawn after each death, and the life counter counts deaths
document_multiplayer_lifeAction: Get close, stop firing, and tap Focus 5 times
document_multiplayer_powerDrops: In most games, normal P drops scale with player count
document_multiplayer_powerTransfer: Get close to a teammate and tap Shoot 5 times
document_multiplayer_deathSummary: Run out of lives to become a ghost, revive at stage clear, and lose the run if everyone becomes a ghost
document_multiplayer_deathbombSummary: Double the time to press Bomb and save a life after being hit
document_multiplayer_tableNote: You can stop here after reading the table. The sections below explain it in more detail.

document_multiplayer_exception_th10: doubles enemy P drops with two players and multiplies them by six with three. Each transfer sends 1.00 Power, and rescue gives about 4.67 seconds of invulnerability.
document_multiplayer_exception_th11: gives Marisa A’s Bomb invulnerability to her alone. Marisa C’s shield protects teammates once it absorbs a hit.
document_multiplayer_exception_th15: keeps P drop counts fixed and increases the value of small P with more players. Ghosts keep any spare lives they banked when rescued.
document_multiplayer_bossSummary: More players means less damage per player
document_multiplayer_controlsSummary: Share dialogue and pause, save replays individually
document_multiplayer_unlockSummary: Characters and stages unlock during co-op
document_multiplayer_differences: For deathbombs, life transfers, and other shared mechanics, see

content_faq:
Frequently asked questions

Thanks to Goan114 for compiling this information, and to everyone who tested and provided feedback.

If the information below does not solve your problem, please contact us through Discord, the QQ group, or GitHub Issues.

What should I do about crashes, lag, black screens, loading problems, or interrupted touch input?

First, try a recommended browser:

Device Recommended browser
Android The latest Edge or Chrome; Via is not recommended
Huawei devices Try the built-in browser; do not use Zhuoyitong or Via
Windows The included Edge, Chrome, or Firefox
Windows 7 and earlier Supermium
Apple devices Any browser

Built-in and other domestic browsers are not recommended. Quark is known to interrupt touch input. If the recommended browsers do not solve the problem, please contact us.

[!NOTE] If an older browser cannot open the home page or the WebGL 2.0 check fails, see the device and browser compatibility guide for Supermium installation and Chrome OpenGL backend instructions.

Where can I find controls, guides, and the story?

  • Controls: Start the game and select “?” in the upper-right corner.
  • Original manuals and story: See the Touhou Project supplementary documents.
  • Strategy guides: See the THBWiki strategy guides, for example to learn about the cherry point system.

If you are unfamiliar with Touhou Project's setting or gameplay, we recommend starting with THBWiki for its thorough, accessible explanations.

Can I save my game?

“Saving” can mean two different things:

Can I resume a run after exiting?

No. As in the original game, you cannot resume a run with its previous lives and other in-game state after exiting. A run takes about 25 minutes on average.

Are clear records and other play data saved?

Yes. Clear records, play time, and other data outside the current run can be saved. Testing confirmed that the score.dat save file is compatible with the original game.

[!WARNING] Save files are specific to each game. For example, th06's score.dat cannot be used in th07.

Will more games be added?

See the game adaptation progress table (Chinese only).

Enable “Preview features” in “Developer options” to check upcoming content.

What if resources will not download?

  1. Make sure you are not using a VPN.
  2. Avoid extensions that take over downloads. Internet Download Manager and similar extensions are known to interfere with resource loading.
  3. If downloading still fails, use the import package.

Once the site has been opened, you can refresh or reopen the launcher even if the server later becomes unavailable or you go offline; nearly all newer browsers support this.

What if multiplayer has problems?

Do not use browser extensions such as WebRTC Control that affect WebRTC.

Multiplayer lag generally has two causes:

  1. Network fluctuations or packet loss. For example, a jump from 50 ms to 200 ms causes noticeable lag; this is normal, as players familiar with Hisoutensoku may know.
  2. Game performance issues.

If your network fluctuates significantly, multiplayer is not recommended. One player's fluctuations can cause everyone in the session to lag.

Support the project

If you like the project, please consider starring it on GitHub.

content_multiplayer:
These co-op rules apply to th06, th07, th08, th10, th11, and th15. See each game’s section for rules specific to that game.

Common rules

Challenge mode

The host can enable Challenge Mode in the room’s game settings. Bombs are set to zero, and the life display counts deaths. Each death drops items and respawns the player as usual, so the run continues.

Boss endurance and player count

Boss HP and stage-script thresholds follow the original game. In co-op, damage dealt to bosses scales with the number of active players.

Active playersDamage multiplier
11
20.75
32/3

When a player becomes a ghost, they are removed from the count and the multiplier adjusts.

Deathbomb window

The deathbomb window is how long you can still press Bomb to save a life after being hit.

In co-op, the deathbomb window is twice as long. The extra time for touch controls still applies.

Death behavior

When a player runs out of lives:

  • They become an uncontrollable ghost that drifts without shooting. Dropped items match the original final-death drops.
  • They can be revived through life transfer.
  • All ghosts revive after a stage clear.

When all players die:

  • A team wipe occurs only after every participant has entered the ghost/revivable state.
  • A synchronized buffer of 180 normal logic frames (about 3 seconds) follows.
  • The run then ends, without continues.

Shared controls and the end of a run

Any player can advance dialogue, pause or resume. Pausing stops simulation for everyone; pressing R while paused restarts the run for everyone.

The run ends after the team-wipe rescue buffer, a full clear or confirmed exit. Endings, result menus, names, replay saving and returning to the title are then controlled independently. After playing the last confirmed frame, spectators can choose a native replay slot, enter a name and save the complete multiplayer replay locally.

Automatic Power-item distribution

  • At the point of collection, red items target the nearest controllable player below full Power; when everyone is full, they target the nearest controllable player. Ties favor the lower seat number.
  • This also applies to collecting below the collection line. The recipient need not cross the line and is not limited by the 20-pixel manual-transfer range.
  • A player below full Power collects normally. If a full-Power player touches a red item, it flies to the nearest teammate below full Power. If everyone is full, collection is normal.
  • A flying item keeps its recipient, but retargets the nearest non-full teammate if that recipient reaches full Power. Ghosts and inactive seats cannot receive red items.
  • When the whole team is full, the game's original full-Power item and scoring rules apply.

Life transfer

To transfer a life:

  1. Move within 20 pixels of a teammate.
  2. The donor must release the fire button and hold at least 1 spare life.
  3. Tap Shift / Focus 5 times, with no more than 24 logic frames (about 0.4 seconds) between presses.

Effects:

  • The donor loses 1 spare life. A controllable recipient receives a homing life item and gains 1 spare life.
  • A ghost recipient revives.
  • Priority is: ghosts, then fewer spare lives, then lower seat number.
  • Holding counts as one press. Shooting, timing out or leaving range resets the count.
  • The third and fourth taps show L 3/5 and L 4/5. The fifth transfers a life; release Focus and tap 5 more times for another transfer.

Additional effects for a revived ghost:

  • Bonus lives alone do not revive ghosts; a teammate must transfer a life, or the stage must end.
  • Power becomes half of that shot type's maximum.
  • Bombs return to the initial count.
  • Revived players gain about 4 seconds of invulnerability. Bullets stay on screen.

Power transfer

To transfer Power:

  • Move within 20 pixels of a teammate.
  • The donor taps fire 5 times.
  • No more than 24 logic frames (about 0.4 seconds) may separate taps.

Effects:

  • A transfer counter appears above the donor from the third tap.
  • The corresponding Power is deducted, and equivalent homing items fly to the recipient.

On the 0–128 Power scale, each transfer sends 20 Power (2 large P items and 4 small P items).

Limits:

  • The donor must hold the full amount required for one transfer.
  • The recipient must be below full Power.
  • Priority is lower Power, then lower seat number.

Unlock synchronization

Extra, characters and practice stages unlock for co-op. These unlocks are temporary. You can save replays.

Rank adjustments

  • Dying or bombing reduces Rank less than in single-player.
  • The reduction is divided by player count.
  • This prevents simultaneous deaths from lowering difficulty too quickly.

Other rules

  • Spell captures and failures are shared.
  • Score- or point-item-based extends are distributed to teammates, subject to individual life caps.
  • In games with bombs, the initial count for each shot type is one below the original, with a minimum of 1.
  • Normal P drops scale with the number of players. Full Power drop counts stay fixed.
  • Mid-stage life and bomb drops use 1× for 2 players and 2× for 3.
  • Nearby teammates and attached effects, including hitboxes and shots, become more transparent.
  • Spell-card portraits are removed; text declarations remain.
  • When one player uses a Bomb, the whole team gains invulnerability.

th06 Embodiment of Scarlet Devil

th07 Perfect Cherry Blossom

Game-specific rules

Power-item distribution

  • When one player reaches full Power, P items on screen become Cherry items and keep moving along their original paths. Once everyone is at full Power, new P drops become Cherry items too.

Cherry+ adjustments

  • With 2 players, the Supernatural Border threshold is 50,000 Cherry+.
  • With 3 players, the threshold is 75,000 Cherry+.
  • Cherry and Cherry+ are shared and Borders activate together. If bombing creates different Border timings, the first player's Border ending ends every player's Border.

Unlocks

  • Phantasm is available in co-op.

th08 Imperishable Night

Game-specific rules

Human/youkai gauge and team state

  • Each player has an independent gauge and human/youkai form. Shots, bombs, deathbombs and team-specific actions follow the selected team.

Familiars

  • Whether a familiar can be attacked, and its visible attackable state, depend on the local player.
  • Familiars never deal contact damage.
  • Bullets fired by familiars still follow the host.

Time orbs and night time

  • The team shares time orbs and night time.

Power items

  • Multiplied P drops spread upward separately. Small P items still give 1 Power; large P items give 8.
  • One full-Power player does not convert P items that other players still need.

Unlocks

  • All routes are available in co-op.

th10 Mountain of Faith

Power items

  • P items on screen turn into point items only after every controllable player reaches full Power.
  • Enemy P drops are twice the original count with 2 players and six times the original count with 3. P spawned directly uses the original count with 2 players and doubles with 3.
  • Each transfer sends 1.00 Power.

Rescue

  • The revived player gains 280 logic frames (about 4.67 seconds) of invulnerability.

th11 Subterranean Animism

Item collection and life fragments

  • With a full communication gauge, you can attract items that have been on screen for at least 40 frames from anywhere on screen. Ordinary items keep following the player who attracted them.
  • Life fragment drops match the original. Every 5 shared fragments give each player 1 life, up to 9 spares. Ghosts can store these lives for rescue.

Bombs and shields

  • Marisa A’s Bomb gives invulnerability to her alone.
  • Marisa C’s shield gives teammates 40 frames of invulnerability when it absorbs a hit. If it expires unused, it refunds half the spent Power and leaves the spell capture intact.

th15 Legacy of Lunatic Kingdom

Game-specific rules

Mode and team accounting

  • Co-op uses Legacy mode.
  • The team shares score, point-item value and graze. Different players can graze the same bullet, and each player’s graze glow is visible.

Life fragments and stored lives

  • Each qualifying chapter reward or collected life fragment adds 1 shared fragment, rather than 2 or 3 based on player count.
  • Chapter rewards use the displayed chapter bonus: default thresholds are 1,250,000 for 2 players and 1,500,000 for 3. Before starting, the host can choose 500,000–5,000,000, in steps of 250,000. The UI also shows the required graze at 100% destruction (threshold ÷ 5,000). The threshold locks at start and does not fall when a teammate becomes a ghost.
  • Normally, 3 shared fragments grant an extend. In Extra, each of the first 5 extends requires 5 fragments; no further fragment extends follow. Each player can hold at most 8 spare lives.
  • Ghosts keep any spare lives earned from fragments when rescued. Death itself grants no fragment. Whole lives, whole Bombs and Bomb fragments belong to their collector.

Life transfer and rescue

  • Rescue grants 280 frames of invulnerability (about 4.67 seconds). Stage-clear revival grants 120 frames (about 2 seconds).

Power values and gifting

  • A small P gives 0.02 Power in a 2-player room or 0.03 Power in a 3-player room. A large P remains 1.00 Power. Room size, not survivors, determines the value; original full-Power scoring remains.
  • P drops use the original counts. Full Power fills the collector’s Power.
  • You need at least 2.00 Power to give one large P, which costs 1.00 Power. If the recipient becomes a ghost, the item becomes an ordinary drop.
  • The third and fourth taps show a large-P icon and count. Life-transfer prompts have priority. No Power-transfer prompt appears below the donation threshold.

Bombs and teammate protection

  • Each life in standard co-op starts with 2 Bombs.
  • Reimu, Marisa and Sanae grant teammates 120 frames of invulnerability when bombing. Each update during the bomb, including the last, tops up teammates to at least 40 frames.
  • Reisen grants at least 30 frames when activating her shield or breaking any layer, including the last. A persistent shield protects only Reisen, not the entire team indefinitely.
  • On mobile, you can keep dragging when Reisen’s shield breaks.

Display, movement and replays

  • Each player sees only their own hitbox, including focused and always-visible hitboxes. Teammate hitboxes remain hidden during fading. Only drawing changes; collision and network state do not.
  • Ghosts gain no graze. Aimed bullets and moving lasers pick controllable players as targets.
  • The 2P panel keeps fragment text and numbers with tighter spacing. The 3P panel removes life/bomb fragment text and numbers but retains icon-fill animations; accounting is unchanged.
  • During mobile dialogue, dragging moves the player when native movement is allowed. Tap to confirm; hold still for 500ms to skip. Dragging does not confirm, skip, auto-fire or double-tap bomb.
  • Multiplayer replays save every seat's character, seed, build identity and confirmed input. Playback requires a compatible multiplayer build; original single-player replays are not accepted. Spell timing uses confirmed logic frames, excluding network waits.
